articles.title: Not Just Stone: 66-Million-Year-Old Dino Bone Yields Original Collagen, Shaking Up Paleontology
articles.summary: A pristine Edmontosaurus sacrum from Hell Creek has delivered the strongest evidence yet that original proteins can survive in dinosaur fossils. Multiple independent tests confirmed collagen fragments, challenging decades of skepticism and opening a new molecular window into the age of dinosaurs.

articles.title: An Ocean on Mars? Shalbatana Vallis Holds Clues in Its Flood-Carved Depths
articles.summary: ESA's Mars Express has delivered stunning new views of Shalbatana Vallis, a 1,300-km outflow channel carved by cataclysmic floods 3.5 billion years ago. The valley's chaotic terrain, volcanic ash, and connection to a possible ancient ocean basin are reshaping our picture of a wetter Mars.

articles.title: Forget Likes, This Social Media Contest Is All About the Crunch
articles.summary: The International Tree Kangaroo Crunch-a-Thon is leveraging adorable munching videos to raise awareness for endangered tree kangaroos. Zoos across the U.S. are competing for most likes and views, with winners announced May 17, ahead of World Tree Kangaroo Day on May 21.
